findings.reason: The protected source is already the canonical optimal graph solution: initialize every observed letter, derive one deduplicated first-difference edge per adjacent word pair, reject reverse-prefix ordering, and use Kahn's algorithm to detect a cycle or emit a valid order. The structure and naming are interview-quality, so no candidate is justified.

Metadata consistently identifies paid-only LeetCode problem 269 and its Python list-to-string contract. The Reference preserves arbitrary valid-order acceptance, impossible-input behavior, all three examples, and all three source constraints; the contract now defines c, a, and e for the branch bounds.

The immutable native source is tied to verified submission 2064293784. It and the app-local source have identical node initialization, adjacent pairing, prefix rejection, first-difference edge deduplication, indegrees, Kahn queue processing, cycle test, and return; only typing and wrapper syntax differ.

The previous largest tier illegally contained 104 words against the 100-word source limit. The replacement 20/50/100-word tiers are legal, preserve sorted prefix-heavy comparisons, and span 80/200/400 total characters. The current source passes at -0.00 relative exponent and 1.06x largest ratio; a correct all-pairs comparison control passes every output but fails only scaling at +0.99 and 32.62x.

The Approach matches the protected source's adjacent first-difference graph and Kahn traversal, and now derives the O(c + e) bound from adjacent comparison participation while accounting for all graph, indegree, queue, result, repeated-word, and isolated-letter state.

The hash-bound paid-only Reference remains verified against its reviewed source evidence, preserving all three examples in order and their explanation presence, all three constraints, and the zero-visual structure.

coverage: all three source-fidelity-verified examples now appear first and in source order as visible samples, including the formerly missing z-before-x example
every correctness and benchmark row uses the alien-dictionary validator so any complete topological order satisfying the inferred constraints is accepted

one 100-character word reaches the exact word-length maximum and exposes all 26 lowercase letters without precedence edges
one hundred repeated one-letter words reach the exact word-count maximum and minimum word length without inventing an edge
all ten expected outputs and the protected outputs matched an independent adjacent first-difference extractor, reverse-prefix check, DFS cycle detector, and precedence-order validator
10,000 seeded random legal-domain word lists agreed on feasibility and produced independently valid orders whenever a solution existed
the protected current source passed all ten correctness rows and all three unchanged benchmark tiers through the real-test engine; benchmark outputs and runtime scaling passed
all ten correctness rows are visible samples or trials, while the unchanged 20, 50, and 100-word workloads remain hidden performance-only benchmarks
